questions.question: Identify the sentence with the INCORRECT usage of adverb.

options.text: Merry was aware of the implications more than her colleagues slightly.
Marsh is an exceptionally talented musician with a bright future.
The presentation was well-organised and effectively delivered.
The novel written by Rahul was harshly critiqued by the readers.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence in Option 1 is incorrect because of the improper placement of the adverb "**slightly**."
 
• In English grammar, adverbs should be positioned to clearly and logically modify the intended word or phrase.
 
• In the sentence "Merry was aware of the implications more than her colleagues slightly," the placement of "**slightly**" at the end of the sentence makes it ambiguous and awkward.
 
• A better construction would be: "**Merry was slightly more aware of the implications than her colleagues."**

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "Marsh is an exceptionally talented musician with a bright future." **– This sentence is grammatically correct and uses the adverb "**exceptionally**" appropriately to modify "talented."
 
• **Option 3: "The presentation was well-organised and effectively delivered."** – This sentence is grammatically correct, with the adverbs "**well-organised**" and "**effectively**" used correctly.
 
• **Option 4: "The novel written by Rahul was harshly critiqued by the readers."** – This sentence is grammatically correct, with the adverb "**harshly**" correctly modifying "critiqued."

questions.question: In the sentence, 'The scientist’s explanation was extremely abstruse', what is a synonym of the word 'abstruse'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Complicated**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"abstruse"** means something that is difficult to understand, obscure, or highly complex in nature. (जटिल या कठिन समझने वाला)

 
 
• **Example: **The professor's abstruse theories on quantum mechanics left the students puzzled.
 
 
 
• **"Complicated"** refers to something that consists of many interconnecting parts or elements, making it difficult to understand or deal with. (जटिल)
 
 
• **Example: **The instructions for assembling the furniture were so complicated that it took hours to complete.
 
 
 
• Hence, "abstruse" and "complicated" are synonyms, as both imply difficulty in understanding.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Complicated**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Clear** (स्पष्ट): Something that is easy to perceive, understand, or interpret.

 
 
• **Example: **Her explanation of the topic was clear and concise, making it easier for everyone to grasp.
 
 
 
• **Obvious** (स्पष्ट या जाहिर): Something that is easily seen, understood, or recognized.
 
 
• **Example: **It was obvious that he was upset after hearing the news.
 
 
 
• **Concise** (संक्षिप्त): Giving a lot of information clearly and in a few words; brief but comprehensive.
 
 
• **Example: **The report was concise yet included all the necessary details.

The new software runs more efficiently than the previous version.

• The correct adverbial form should be "less thoroughly" because it modifies the verb "completed" and refers to the manner of completing the assignment.
 
• Adverbs are typically used to modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs, and they often end in "-ly" when describing the manner of an action.

• "Two" would not make sense in this context, as the sentence does not specify the toddler asking for a specific quantity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

• **Option 3: "none"** – Incorrect, as it implies no cake was given at all.
 
• **Option 4: "two"** – Incorrect, as there is no reference to the toddler asking for a specific quantity.
